plateNote: Read on the promoted plate (art/staging/room-14/plate-02/candidate-1920x864.png, room-14 attempt 3, the scattered stones, the standard 20:9 crop -- frame.json). Every rect below was read off that picture with a grid over it.
walkableNote: THE GRASS BEFORE THE STONES. The lowest boards' feet are at y 530, so the band starts at 560-575 and every board is behind it. At the left the gate's posts and the fence stand to y 680-720, so the band there starts below them (y 735). Mott's obelisk stands IN the band: it is an obstacle, with the grass behind it, so Thad passes in front of it and is never drawn across it.

obstacles.note: Mott's stone and its lilies (x 540-715, foot at y 795) and the grass behind them: he walks round in front, never behind, so nothing needs a clip plane.

Errata 233: the hearse's wheels and Grievance's hooves (procession_hearse, feet at y 792, x 740-1690), while the procession is stalled. He walks in front of the hitch or behind it, never through it. The floor is built twice, with and without it (tools/compile-room.mjs, gated obstacles).

scaling.note: ROOM 14'S DEPTH, FROM THE MAN THE MASTER PAINTED. The composition master drew Thad about 240 tall with his feet at source y 830, which is 303 at y 834 in this plate's frame. The painting is nearly flat in depth -- the back boards (y 170-295) are drawn the size of the front ones (y 395-530) -- so the curve is too: 285 at the band's far edge, 305 at its near.

entrances.note: In by the gate, at left: the map leads here.
Down from the funeral at the plot beside Pike's, at the back right (errata 99 G).

hotspotsNote: Generous over the thing the player sees (ruling 32). THE NINETEEN is the scatter of boards between Mott's stone and Pike's (one hotspot, read along, doc 54). PIKE'S MARKER is the right-most board at the back, at the hill's crest; the plot beside it, to its right, is PIKE'S NEIGHBOR while it is dug and MY OWN PLOT after the funeral (errata 87 D). Errata 185: THE FENCE, the rails left of the gate. Errata 233 (doc 110 section 2): while the procession is stalled at the gate, THE HEARSE and GRIEVANCE, AT THE GATE over the hitch (content/ambient/procession-hearse.json, art/actors/room-14-hearse-grievance.png: reference/act3-hearse/handback.md), right of Mott's obelisk, REVEREND SOWERBY, AT THE GATE, THE UNDERTAKER and THE MOURNERS over their figures (procession_*).

THE GATE.note: Doc 20 and errata 43: Boot Hill is reached by the map, and its gate leads back to it. Doc 49's CLOSE is its one line. NO DOCUMENT WRITES THE GATE A LOOK OR LISTEN (doc 54: 'THE GATE is the room's exit'), so it is a stub exit as the records room's door is (errata 72 F, doc 36 Q157); the gate works, and its LOOK and LISTEN wait for lines. Errata 189: its LOOK and LISTEN are doc 106's (linesFrom), and it is no longer a stub.

PIKE'S NEIGHBOR.note: Doc 20: Room 31, the funeral, is reached from Boot Hill once the executor is named (E6). The open plot beside Pike is where it is held, so from E6 until the funeral is done the plot is the way up to it; its words stay on PIKE'S NEIGHBOR, which is hidden meanwhile (errata 99 G). Errata 233 (doc 110 section 2, THE WAY ON): from E6 until the ride (T_RODE_UP) the procession is stalled at the gate, and the way up refuses with doc 110's line; the ride itself is how he gets there.

obstaclesNote: Mott's obelisk only. Errata 233: the hitch, while the procession is stalled.

lamps.note: The town's lamps below the hill, at the left. A slow, faint breath (invariant 9): nothing on the hill moves for a reason.

defaultVerbsNote: Errata 28b. Every marker here is looked at on a bare click.

occlusion.note: NO PLANE: every board's foot is above the band, and Mott's stone is an obstacle with its ground behind it.

props.note: Doc 05: the grave dug in Act III for Thad, open, the marker painted in Frame's spelling -- so from the obituary (E5) until the funeral. Room-14 operation 4's changed pixels (tools/art/room14-props.py).
Doc 05 Part Two-B: after the funeral, the headboard, the grass starting over it, a tuning peg on top. Composed from operations 4 and 5 (tools/art/room14-compose.py, errata 87 F).

onEnterSay.note: Doc 57 C3: 'Room 14, Boot Hill -- entering ends the day. The service is just over.' The line plays and the day clears; it can be held again (errata 87 C).

onEnterSetNote: Doc 57 C3: 'If T_SHENG_TASK is set and D4 is not done, Sowerby is at the gate with the plate (D4). Then T_FUNERAL_DAY clears ... and Sowerby is back in his church.' He stands at the gate for the visit that ends the day (T_PLATE_AT_GATE), and is gone the next time. Errata 233 (doc 110 section 2, States and flags): until scene B is built, the first entry once the funeral can be reached (E6, the obituary, before the funeral and the ride) stalls the procession at the gate.

onEnterScenes.note: Doc 57 D4: on the funeral day the Reverend has a full plate, at the foot of Boot Hill -- the exchange, then THE LINEN MONEY. Plays after the day's own line. His figure is content/ambient/sowerby-gate.json.
Doc 110 section 2, ARRIVING: said on the entry that stalls the procession, so once.

hotspotWalkToNote: Errata 233: where Thad stands to examine the procession's figures, in front of the hitch and between the people, so he never stands on one.
docBlocksNote: Errata 233, doc 110 section 2, THE LINES: TALK TO each of the procession, the prayer asked for, and USE or OPEN THE HEARSE (refused with the town watching; during the prayer, Thad climbs in: T_RODE_UP, E6b, THE RIDE over black, and Room 31). The words are read from doc 110 by tools/compile-room.mjs (docBlock).
